ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, point A is at the lower left, and point B is at the lower right. Terminal A is connected to the left-side common node, and this node divides into two upper and lower branches: the upper branch contains resistor R1 and leads to the right-side common node; the lower branch contains resistor R2, then passes through switch K, and leads to the same right-side common node. This right-side common node then passes through resistor R3 in series to point B. Reasoning: Let R1 = R2 = R3 = R. When switch K is open, the lower branch is disconnected, R2 does not participate in conduction, and the only path from A to B is R1 and then R3 in series, so R_open = R1 + R3 = 2R. When switch K is closed, R1 and R2 are connected between the same pair of nodes, therefore they are in parallel; this parallel combination is then in series with R3, so R_closed = (R1 || R2) + R3 = R/2 + R = 3R/2. The required ratio is R_open / R_closed = 2R / (3R/2) = 4/3 ≈ 1.3.

raw_record.question_text: In the circuit shown in the figure, given \(R_1 = R_2 = R_3\), what is the ratio of the equivalent resistance between points A and B when switch K is open to when it is closed?

method.method_draft: Let each resistor be R, as stated. From the image, with K open the R2 branch is interrupted, so the only path from A to the right junction is through R1, then through R3 to B: R_open = R1 + R3 = 2R. With K closed, R1 and R2 connect between the same two nodes, so they are parallel, and this parallel pair is in series with R3: R_closed = (R1 || R2) + R3 = R/2 + R = 3R/2. Compute the requested ratio R_open/R_closed = 2R/(3R/2) = 4/3, reported as about 1.3.

method.method_draft: Assign all resistors value R and apply a test voltage V between A and B. For K open, the image shows only one complete path A -> R1 -> right junction -> R3 -> B, so the input current is I_open = V/(2R). For K closed, current entering from A can split through equal R1 and R2 branches before recombining and passing through R3. Equivalently, the voltage drop across the A-to-junction part corresponds to two equal branch currents, giving the same total as a resistance R/2 in that section, so I_closed = V/(R/2 + R) = V/(3R/2). Since R_eq = V/I, the requested ratio is R_open/R_closed = I_closed/I_open = [V/(3R/2)]/[V/(2R)] = 4/3, approximately 1.3.
